transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess what brought me in is I feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit and idle. And with the new setup at work, it’s been harder to hide that or work around it.
Can you describe what you mean by always moving from one thing to the next? Do you feel physically restless or find it hard to stay still?

Yeah, physically restless, I’d say. If I’m sitting through a training video or some slow appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I’ll want to stand up, stretch, shift around, or at least be doing something with my hands. It’s not dramatic, but it’s hard to just sit still and do nothing.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you try not to, or does your mind often feel like it's racing with thoughts you can't slow down?

I’m not sure I’d call it worrying, exactly. My mind can feel busy, but I don’t know that it’s always worry about different things. It’s more like I have a lot going on in my head, and I’m not always great at shutting it off.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks, especially ones that require sustained attention, like reading a report or following through on detailed instructions?

Yes, that happens. Like in the longer coaching meetings, or if I’m trying to read through a new procedure, I’ll start off okay. But after a few minutes I realize my eyes have kept moving, or I’ve been sitting there listening, but I didn’t really take in what was said.
Do you experience this same restlessness and difficulty focusing in places other than work, like at home or when you’re out with friends?

Yes, it happens outside work too. At home, if I try to read or sit through a movie with my wife, I’m okay for a little bit, but then I start shifting around or making comments, or I’ll get up to grab something. Quiet things that are supposed to be relaxing don’t usually hold me for very long.
Have you felt this way for a long time, or is this something that started more recently? I mean, when you think back, were you already this way as a kid, or did it come on more in adulthood?

It’s been around a long time. I don’t think it started with this job or anything recent. Looking back to grade school, I remember teachers saying I was bright, but careless. They’d write that I talked out of turn or had to be reminded to stay on my work. So yeah, it was there when I was a kid too.
Do you often act on impulse, like saying or doing something without thinking it through first, or feeling like you need to do something right away without waiting?

Yes, I do that sometimes. I don’t mean to be rude, but at work if I hear coworkers talking through a customer problem, I’ll jump in with an answer before they’re even finished, or before anyone asked me. It’s like I feel like I need to get it out right then.

Do you find that these symptoms of restlessness, trouble focusing, and acting quickly without thinking happen more often in situations where you're not under pressure or feeling anxious, or do they seem to only come up when you're stressed or in high-pressure moments?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I notice it when I’m stressed, but I don’t think I’ve paid close enough attention to whether it’s only then or not. It just kind of happens, and I haven’t really sorted out a pattern.
Can you think of a time when you were completely relaxed and not under any pressure, where you still noticed the same restlessness, trouble focusing, or acting without thinking?

Yeah, I can think of that. Like at home, if I’m trying to read or if my wife and I are watching a movie, there’s no real pressure there. But after a while I’ll start shifting around, making comments, or I’ll get up to go do something. It’s not like I’m anxious, I just don’t sit with it very long.

Can you think of a time when you were not at work or home, like when you were out in public or at a social event, where you noticed the same restlessness, trouble focusing, or acting without thinking?

Yeah, I notice it in public too. Like if I’m sitting through a training video somewhere or waiting through a slow appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I’ll want to stand up, stretch, or at least do something with my hands. It’s not a big dramatic thing, but I definitely feel restless just sitting there.
